Main System: The largest system is the Main System that serves the cold rooms and the water chillers. Main System is composed of fixed and portable equipment. Fixed equipment includes high- and low-pressure receivers, ammonia pumps, cold room evaporators, water chillers and surge drums, evaporative condenser,  ammonia detection, control systems, and diffusion tank. Portable equipment includes three skid-mounted screw compressors. Two of the screw compressors ships to Salinas, CA facility for summer operations. The other screw compressor (AHRC 1205A) stays on site all year. Main System is operated seasonally from November to April. The ammonia charge of the Main System including the portable equipment is approximately 15,000 lbs.

Vacuum Cooling System (RT 12/14): Vacuum cooling system comprises of two (2) 12-pallet (half-car) vacuum tubes w/ surge drums on top of each tube (flooded system) and one refrigeration trailer. The Refrigeration Trailer consists of two screw compressors, one high-pressure receiver, and one evaporative condenser. Vacuum Cooling System has approximately 3,000 lbs. of ammonia. Facility also leases a vacuum cooling system (T-127), which operates as a standalone system and consist of a high-side trailer and half-car vacuum tube. High side trailers have evaporative condenser, screw compressor(s) and high-pressure receiver. Vacuum Cooling System has approximately 1,200 lbs. of ammonia. Vacuum Cooling Systems are operated seasonally from November to April. At the end of the season, all vacuum cooling system equipment ships to Salinas, CA facility for summer operations, from April to November.

The facility pumps down all the ammonia in the Main System to the high-pressure and low pressure receivers during the off season and all the ammonia in the vacuum cooling system to on-site nurse tanks.

1. Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies

GreenGate Fresh facility conducts inspection procedures to review refrigeration equipment prior to startup and during operations. These procedures identify potential sources of release and equipment corrections required to prevent these releases. On-site personnel and certified refrigeration contractors review the equipment as required. On-site personnel provide initial emergency response.
On-site personnel will make a preliminary assessment in the event of a release and will contact refrigeration contractor. No emergency operations will be performed that are beyond the capabilities of the operators or other on-site personnel. Local fire and police departments with mutual aid response will provide emergency response for a major release event. Refrigeration contractors will be on-call to provide emergency response. Emergency response training will be conducted yearly for current employees and as required for new employees. Records will be kept of all training performed at the site for a minimum of five (5) years.

2. Stationary Source and Regulated Substances Handled

GreenGate Fresh uses anhydrous ammonia as a refrigerant in their operations. Drawings in Chapter 8 - Appendix 8.1 show the facility location map and site plan.

GreenGate Fresh has over 10,000 lbs. of ammonia in any single refrigeration system. Anhydrous ammonia is used as a refrigerant in product storage cooling, vacuum cooling, and water chilling operations. There are three (3) separate refrigeration systems (processes) at the facility. These processes are (1) Main System, and (2) Vacuum Cooling Systems. The Main System is the largest single system with ammonia quantity of approximately 15,000 lbs., which is above the federal TQ of 10,000 lbs. Each Vacuum Cooling System has less than 10,000 lbs. of ammonia. The facility has no machinery room housing the refrigeration equipment.

Each system is a single stage closed loop ammonia refriger

ain system and vacuum cooling system equipment except the cold room evaporators are located outdoors.

The total quantity of ammonia currently at the site is approximately 19,120 lbs. 

The compressors have safety cutouts that will shut down the compressors upon detection of unsafe operating conditions. All pressure vessels and the compressors are protected against high-pressure situations by safety relief valves. All low side vessels that are connected directly to the suction of compressor is installed with high level float switches that shuts down compressor upon detection of high liquid level in the vessel. All cold storage warehouses are installed with ammonia sensors that triggers an alarm upon detection of ammonia vapor in the vicinity of the sensor. Refrigeration control system sends alarms to refrigeration manager in case of emergency situation or any high pressure, high temperature or ammonia detection.

Updated refrigeration drawings are located in Appendix 8.1-Refrigeration System Drawings. International Institute of Ammonia Refrigeration (IIAR) "Ammonia Refrigeration Safety Inspection Checklists," located in Appendix 12.1, describe equipment details.

The refrigeration systems at this facility are a single-stage vapor compression cycle. In general, the process chemistry for each system is described in Chapter 8.3.

Anhydrous ammonia (NH3) is a gas in its natural state and is extremely irritating to mucous membranes and lung tissue. The gas is pungent and may be suffocating as shortness of breath and labored breathing can develop if inhaled. Prolonged inhalation of high concentrations may cause bronchitis and/or pneumonia, with some residual reduction in pulmonary functions. Repeated or prolonged contact of high concentrations of ammonia to the skin can cause frostbite, redness, pain and serious skin burn. See Appendix 8.4 for Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for anhydrous ammonia.

3. General Accidental Release Prevention Program

GreenGate Fresh maintains a rel

ease prevention program to eliminate or minimize releases. The program includes regular inspections, monitoring equipment and logging conditions, scheduled maintenance, and operator training. There is a program to analyze releases for ways to prevent a similar future release, see Chapter 16-Incident Investigation.

The ammonia refrigeration system has specific safety procedures to prevent a release. Operators  are trained for safe operation of the refrigeration system. Contractor performs all maintenance and inspections on the system and  Ammonia detectors are installed in all refrigerated rooms. Personnel will automatically be notified if any detector exceeds its set point. Monitoring is done 24 hours per day. All of the relief valves at the main system and the vacuum cooling system are tied into an ammonia diffusion tanks (one for each system) to prevent high-pressure releases to ambient.

4. Five-Year Accident History

GreenGate Fresh had no releases of anhydrous ammonia in the last 5 years that resulted in deaths, injuries, or significant property damage on site, or known offsite deaths, injuries, evacuations, sheltering in place, property damage, or environmental damage.

5. Emergency Response Program

GreenGate Fresh facility is a "Non-Responding" facility. Facility only responds to situations that are within their capabilities. These may include, emergency shutdown, equipment isolation and pumping down the system. No emergency response actions or site clean-up that are beyond the capabilities of the refrigeration personnel will be performed. In case of an emergency, incident will be reported immediately to the RMP Program Coordinator. The RMP Program Coordinator is responsible for assisting county emergency responders upon arrival on site. This may include contacting emergency response agencies, schools, daycare centers, and acute care facilities that may be affected by the release. The RMP Program Coordinator will also be responsible for evacuation of employ

ees if necessary and for coordination with community emergency responders if off-site evacuations are required.

6. Planned Changes to Improve Safety

Recommended corrective actions to mitigate the potential for an accidental ammonia release are proposed on the tables located in RMP Binder Chapter 0.0. The table items result from recommendations made during the Process Hazard Analysis, a Code Compliance Review, Seismic Review, and a Safety Inspection performed by a qualified person. Some recommendation items in the recommendation table originate from multiple codes but are listed only once. Specific facility areas and systems categorize recommendations resulting from the Safety Inspection; some of which may repeat general Process Hazard Analysis and Code Compliance Review items. 
Based on the severity of the hazards identified, implementation deadlines are also recommended. All refrigeration equipment is well maintained and operated in a safe manner by trained personnel. Operating, maintenance, training, and safety procedures will be formalized with improved written documentation.
